newsitem.title: USA: NYS MTA advances $400 mln bond sale due low yields.
newsitem.headline: NYS MTA advances $400 mln bond sale due low yields.

text.p: The Metropolitan Transportation Authority of the State of New York on Friday said that it planned to advance a $400 million sale of new money bonds to August 12 due to the recent drop in yields.

Kim Paparello, deputy director of finance, told Reuters by telephone "We were supposed to do the regularly scheduled new money sale in late August or early September and we just thought the market was so good we would try to move it up."

The new money sale, which would raise funds for the authority's capital program, would be split equally between its transit and commuter arms. Smith Barney will take its turn as senior manager for the negotiated sale, with Bear Stearns and PaineWebber backstopping.
The Authority also might sell from $50 million to $100 million of refunding bonds as part of the same offering, Paparello said.

The yield on the bellwether, 30-year Treasury bond on Friday stood at 6.46 percent, down sharply from 6.54 percent on Monday. The big drop in yields has prompted speculation that municipal issuers increasingly would decide to go ahead with offerings, including refundings, because they now are economical.
